headline: USTBL proxy+implementation verified on Etherscan; EUTBL proxy implementations unconfirmed; sole Trail of Bits audit is ~19 months stale with no follow-up evidence found

findings.text: USTBL proxy (0xe4880249, Ethereum) is verified on Etherscan (ABI source: 'etherscan') and resolves to implementation 0x15EA0EC460a0E6847EC0AA8D50A84B3A51B95f74, which is itself verified on Etherscan with a full UUPS token ABI (proxiableUUID returns ERC-1967 slot). EUTBL proxy (0xa0769f7a, Ethereum) is registered with ABI source 'sourcify' but defipunkd surfaces only the bare ERC1967Proxy ABI (3 events, no view methods) and does not expose an implementation address — implementation verification status is unconfirmed this run. EUTBL proxy on Arbitrum (0xcbeb195) is ABI-source 'etherscan' but similarly shows only the minimal proxy ABI with no implementation surfaced.
Protocol GitHub org is 'spiko-tech'. Source-to-repo correspondence was not confirmed this run — no GitHub source file fetch succeeded. Recorded as unknown.

One audit link is pinned: Trail of Bits, 2023-10-spiko-securityreview.pdf. The GitHub file page confirms the file exists (662 KB) and is dated October 2023 by filename. The PDF content was not fetched this run (fetch budget exhausted), so exact contracts in scope and commit hash are unknown. The audit predates this analysis by approximately 19 months with no follow-up review found.
Trail of Bits is a broadly recognized Solidity audit firm per the checklist. The audit firm designation satisfies V4.

Post-audit drift cannot be assessed: the audit PDF content was not fetched this run, and no GitHub commit SHA was pinned. The USTBL implementation exposes UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION='5.0.0' (OpenZeppelin v5), which postdates a typical October 2023 audit scope. Whether changes are material or covered by a follow-up audit is unknown.

USTBL implementation 0x15EA0EC4 is verified independently on Etherscan (ABI source: 'etherscan'). EUTBL proxy implementations on both Ethereum and Arbitrum were not surfaced by defipunkd in this run; their verification status is unconfirmed. The address_book entry 0xa47c8bf3 (labelled 'Permission Manager') resolves on-chain to 'Wrapped UST Token' (Terra-era UST bridge token), not a Spiko contract — this is a mislabelled address_book entry.

steelman.red: The EUTBL proxy implementations are not surfaced or confirmed as verified in this run, and a verified proxy with an unverified implementation is effectively unverified under V6; if the EUTBL implementations are unverified, a red grade applies to those contracts.
steelman.orange: While USTBL proxy and implementation are both confirmed verified on Etherscan and the auditor (Trail of Bits) is recognized, the sole audit is ~19 months old with OZ v5 deployed (postdating a 2023 review), the EUTBL implementation verification is unconfirmed, and no follow-up audit was found — a classic partial-verification / stale-audit orange profile.
steelman.green: Both USTBL proxy and implementation are verified on Etherscan, Trail of Bits is a top-tier auditor, and the contracts are upgradeable UUPS tokens whose logic is transparent on-chain; if EUTBL implementations are also verified (likely, given the same ABI pattern), the bytecode posture is strong.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: (1) USTBL proxy + implementation are confirmed verified, satisfying V1/V6 for that pair, but EUTBL proxy implementations on Ethereum and Arbitrum were not surfaced this run, leaving their verification unconfirmed; (2) the single Trail of Bits audit (October 2023) predates the analysis by ~19 months and the deployed implementation reports OpenZeppelin v5 compatibility, suggesting the codebase evolved post-audit; (3) no follow-up or differential audit was found. These two factors — partial implementation verification and stale audit scope — jointly meet the orange criteria without meeting green.

protocol_metadata.about: Spiko is a Paris-based MiFID-licensed investment firm that tokenizes European and US Treasury bill money market funds as permissioned ERC-20 tokens (EUTBL, USTBL) on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, Base, and other chains. Users subscribe to and redeem fund shares through the Spiko platform, earning daily interest accrued from short-duration government securities. Token transfers are restricted to KYC-approved addresses enforced by an on-chain authority/permission manager contract. The protocol is regulated under EU UCITS and MiFID rules, with client assets held off-chain at CACEIS Bank (Crédit Agricole group).
